sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the service of turning from evil and doing good is perfected through Torah study, especially the inner dimension of Torah which connects the hidden essence of Israel with the hidden essence of the Holy One, and that the revelation of Atzmus is specifically in the inner Torah, particularly as revealed in Chassidus.

translations.translation: And from this it is understood,
that in order for the service of "turn from evil"
(the aspect of Nefesh)
and "do good"
(the aspect of Ruach)
to be as required,
it is through the occupation with Torah
(the aspect of Neshamah),
and particularly through occupation with the inner dimension of Torah,
with the secrets of Torah and the secrets of secrets,

for the aspect of the inner dimension of Torah, called the hidden aspect of Torah, is that which connects and unites the aspect of the hidden aspect of Israel with the aspect of the hidden aspect of the Holy One, blessed be He.
And although the drawing down of the Atzmus [Essence] that is in Torah is in all parts of Torah,
even in the revealed part of Torah,
and even in the reading of the letters of Torah
(even when one does not know what is being said)
as explained in the Hemshech of Ta"aR"B [5662],
nevertheless, it is explained there that the revelation of Atzmus is specifically in the inner dimension of Torah
[for the inner aspect of Abba is the inner aspect of Atik,
and therefore the revelation of the inner aspect of Atik is specifically in the inner aspect of Abba].
And particularly in the inner dimension of Torah as it was revealed in the Torah of Chassidus by the Baal Shem Tov,
and all the more so as it was revealed by the Alter Rebbe in the Chassidus of Chabad,
in a manner of "they shall be sustained."
And through occupation with Torah,
and particularly with the inner dimension of Torah,
there is also an elevation in the service of "turn from evil" and "do good."
Now, just as the repentance of "Shuva [Israel]... for you have stumbled in your iniquity" is not about sins in their simple sense, G-d forbid,
since all Jews are presumed to be kosher,
and particularly after the repentance of the month of Elul and the days of Selichos,
and especially after Rosh HaShanah when all Jews are vindicated in judgment,
to the extent that even on Erev Rosh HaShanah they already know with certainty that they will be vindicated in judgment,
for "Your people are all righteous,"
and particularly after the shofar blowing, when the matter of wealth is accomplished
[as is known, that which our sages said,
"She becomes wealthy at its conclusion" is immediately after the shofar blowing],
and the repentance of Shabbos Shuva
(after Rosh HaShanah)
is only regarding the selfhood of "there is one who loves"
(and within this itself—in the ultimate subtlety),
as above
(section 7),
so too is it regarding the repentance of "do good" and "seek peace,"
that although these matters were also done previously,
the repentance of Shabbos Shuva is that the fulfillment of the mitzvos should be with even greater hiddur [beautification],
and so too regarding occupation with Torah and particularly with the inner dimension of Torah as revealed in the Torah of Chassidus, and especially in the Chassidus of Chabad,
including also the matter of "may your wellsprings spread forth outward,"
until "the earth will be filled with knowledge of the L-rd as the waters cover the sea,"
that it should be a year of Torah, a year of repentance, and a year of prayer,
and likewise all the blessings of all the letters,
a year of light, a year of blessing, a year of redemption, etc.,
and particularly—the primary blessing,
the complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach, speedily and truly.
